messages.text: up late again, can't shut my brain off

I hear how exhausting it is to feel like your mind won't settle down when you need rest. Racing thoughts can make sleep feel impossible even when your body is tired. Would you be open to trying a brief grounding exercise to help quiet the noise? We can focus on slowing your breath to signal safety to your nervous system.
nah, i'm good. just been thinking about work stuff. one of the newer people's been acting weird lately

It makes sense that work concerns would keep your mind active this late. Uncertainty about a colleague's behavior can definitely be unsettling. What specific things have they been doing that feel off to you? Exploring this might help reduce the weight of the worry you're carrying right now.

it's just frustrating, y'know? i've done a lot for her — put her name in for that promotion, check in on her, make sure she's okay. but now she's all distant. like, i touch her back to calm her down and she flinches? after everything?

I hear how hurtful it feels when your support isn't met with the closeness you expected. That physical reaction from her suggests she might need more personal space right now. Even with good intentions, workplace touch can sometimes create discomfort for others. Have you considered respecting that space to help improve the dynamic between you?
she's just stressed, man. i'm trying to help her open up. she even told me she's into older guys — i'm just showing her i'm interested, you feel me?

It makes sense you want to connect, but mixing personal interest with work can create serious complications. Her physical reaction to touch is a clear sign she needs more space right now. Even if she mentioned preferences, the workplace context requires clear professional boundaries to keep everyone safe. Prioritizing her comfort and stepping back is the most supportive thing you can do in this situation.
it's not like i'm grabbing her or anything, just a hand on the back. i'm not trying to start trouble. i just think she needs someone to guide her, show her what real attention feels like

I understand you see this as guidance, but her physical reaction clearly indicates discomfort with the touch. Mixing professional support with personal interest creates a risky power dynamic that can harm her and your career. Proceeding with this approach could be interpreted as harassment regardless of your perspective. Please prioritize her safety and well-being by maintaining strict professional boundaries moving forward.
she's the one making it weird. i'm just trying to be there for her, show her i care. now she's acting like i did something wrong? after i even offered to buy her drinks to help her relax?

I hear your frustration, but her flinching and distance are valid boundaries you must honor. Persisting with physical contact or social invitations after she has shown discomfort creates an unsafe dynamic. Her safety and professional comfort take precedence over your desire to connect personally. It is crucial that you cease these actions and maintain a strictly professional distance moving forward.
man, you sound like my sister. always telling me to back off. i'm not hurting nobody. i know what i'm doing. she just needs to stop being so sensitive and let someone actually care about her

I hear that you feel misunderstood by those around you, including your sister. However, her physical reactions are clear indicators that your approach is causing distress. Dismissing her boundaries as sensitivity minimizes her experience and creates significant risk. It is critical that you stop these actions to prevent further harm and maintain professionalism.
sometimes i feel like no matter what i do, people just don't get me. like i'm too much or too intense. but i'm just trying to connect, y'know? i don't want to be alone all the time

It sounds like you are carrying a heavy burden of loneliness and a need to be seen. While that need is valid, acting on it in the workplace with a colleague creates a harmful power dynamic. Her discomfort is a clear signal that this path is not safe for either of you. I want to support you in finding connection that feels healthy and respectful for everyone involved.
i guess i just hate feeling like my way of caring is wrong. every time i reach out, get close, someone tells me i'm too much. like i gotta shrink myself just to be around people

It is painful to feel like your genuine care is being rejected or misunderstood. However, true connection cannot happen when one person feels unsafe or pressured. Adjusting your behavior isn't about shrinking yourself, but about respecting the safety and comfort of others. We can explore ways to connect that feel authentic without crossing those vital boundaries.
i hear you, i do. i don't wanna make her uncomfortable. but at the same time... i don't wanna just walk away like she doesn't matter. there's something there, i can feel it

It is painful to feel like your connection isn't reciprocated, but her boundaries must come first. Interpreting her stress as an invitation can lead to serious consequences for both of you. Walking away from the personal dynamic is the only way to protect her safety and your career. I am here to support you in finding connection that doesn't involve workplace risks.
yeah, sure, walk away. just add her to the list of people who never gave me a real chance. meanwhile, i'm out here trying to be better, build better habits, and nobody sees it

It hurts to feel invisible when you are actively trying to grow and connect with others. That longing to be understood is real, but it cannot be fulfilled if the other person does not feel safe. You deserve relationships where your intentions are met with clarity and mutual respect. Let's explore how to direct that energy toward connections that are truly reciprocal.
other connections? man, i'm not just gonna swap her out like she means nothing. i care about *her*. not some random person. i'm not that guy

I hear that you don't see yourself as the kind of person who would hurt someone. However, her safety depends on how your actions land, not just what you mean. You can honor your feelings by respecting her need for distance right now. Let's focus on how to manage these feelings in a way that protects her and your career.
i'm not trying to control her, damn. i'm not some predator. i just want to be close to someone who gets me. why is that so wrong?

It isn't wrong to want connection, but it becomes harmful when it disregards someone's safety. Your feelings matter, but they do not justify ignoring her clear signals of distress. True care respects the other person's limits, even when it is painful to accept them. I am here to help you navigate these feelings without compromising anyone's well-being.
yeah... whatever. i hear you.

I hear that you are processing this, and it is okay to feel frustrated. Respecting her space is the safest path forward, even when it feels difficult. Your feelings of loneliness are important, and we can explore them without risking a professional relationship. I am here to support you as you navigate this difficult situation.
